settings.heading: Foam, not filling.
settings.body:
A lot of dog beds are filled with loose fibre or shredded offcuts. They feel plump in the shop and are flat by March, at which point your dog is sleeping on the floor with a cover over it.

Our orthopaedic beds are built on foam instead. On many, memory foam on top contours to hip and shoulder while a profiled egg-crate layer underneath spreads their weight, so it doesn't compress to the floor. Each bed's page says exactly how it's built, and the fibre-filled nest beds say so too.

settings.heading: Why they're named after fells and dales.
settings.body:
Borrowdale, Coniston, Grasmere, Windermere. The range takes its names from the places the walking gets done at weekends, which is also where most of the thinking about these beds happened.

Each one is built around a sleeping style rather than a price point. Curlers get walls. Sprawlers get surface. Old joints get foam that doesn't bottom out. Where a bed is fibre-filled rather than foam, its page says so.

settings.question: How do I know which size to get?
settings.answer: Measure nose to base of tail while they're lying down, then add about 20cm. Between two sizes? Go up. Every bed's page lists the sleeping area, breeds and weight for each size, and the Bed Finder picks a size for you. Still unsure? Send us a photo of them asleep.

settings.question: What's inside, and isn't firmer better?
settings.answer: It depends on the bed, so each page says exactly what's inside: memory foam, egg-crate foam, crumb memory foam, fibre or mesh. Firmness is only how a bed feels on day one; what matters is whether it still holds them up a few winters on. Loose fibre packs down under a dog's weight. Foam keeps its shape far longer, which is why the memory foam beds carry a [years]-year guarantee on the core.

settings.question: What if my dog just won't use it?
settings.answer: Then it comes back. Some dogs claim a new bed the first night; some take a fortnight. Put it where they already sleep, with a blanket that smells of home on top. You've got [nights] nights. If it still isn't right, we collect it free from the UK mainland and refund in full. Full terms are in our [returns_policy].

settings.question: Will it help a dog with arthritis or stiff hips?
settings.answer: A supportive bed spreads their weight so pressure isn't concentrated on hips, elbows and shoulders. But a bed is for comfort, not a treatment, and it won't replace veterinary care. What it can change is the surface they spend twelve to fourteen hours a day on.

settings.question: When will it arrive, and what does delivery cost?
settings.answer: Our own stock is dispatched in [dispatch] working days, then standard delivery takes [transit] working days, free on orders over £[threshold] and £4.99 below. Express is £6.99. Every bed's page shows its dates before you order. A few beds ship from our partner warehouse and take longer; their pages say so.

settings.question: Can I actually wash it?
settings.answer: On most of the range the cover comes off and washes, following the care label sewn into it. Beds with a coated, waterproof cover are wiped clean instead. Each bed's page says which applies, and whether it has a waterproof inner liner that keeps accidents off the foam.
